title: Passing the list operator
description: You can reuse one recursive list function with multiplication or addition.

steps.description: oplist takes an operator op and a list L. For a one-element list, you return that element directly.
For a longer list, op combines the first element with the recursive result for the rest. You pass the same operator into each recursive call.

steps.question: How do the two oplist calls differ in their results?
steps.answer: Multiplication produces 48 from 2, 4 and 6. Addition produces 12 from the same list.

steps.description: You see 48, 12 and 48 in the output. The final apply call passes the list's elements as arguments to multiplication.
